findings.title: Reconciliation model never written by any code path -- no repair for gateway.verify()-succeeded-but-crash-before-commit gap
findings.note: User chose the full job. New ReconciliationService sweeps stale settleable payments that hold an authority every 10 minutes (@nestjs/schedule, the one dependency added this pass), re-verifies each against Zarinpal, writes a Reconciliation row for every discrepancy and repairs it through PaymentsService.settleVerified -- the same path a real callback takes, so fulfil/returnCapture rules stay in one place. Single-flight across instances via the existing Redis lock; dev_ authorities skipped so the local simulator does not auto-fulfil abandoned checkouts; agreeing payments deliberately write no row. NOT live-verified end to end: exercising the repair path needs a real ZARINPAL_MERCHANT_ID, which this environment does not have.

findings.title: File uploads size-capped but no request-rate limit
Access tokens not invalidated on suspension/role change
findings.regression_test: apps/api/src/common/guards/access-token.guard.spec.ts + apps/api/src/modules/admin/admin.service.spec.ts (revocation publish points); live-verified: a seeded student's already-issued token went 200 -> 401 the moment an admin suspended them, with other users unaffected
findings.note: User chose to implement revocation. New TokenRevocationService writes a per-user seconds-since-epoch marker to Redis (revoked:user:<id>, 1h TTL > the 15m token lifetime); AccessGuard rejects any token whose iat <= that marker. Published by updateUserStatus (non-ACTIVE only), setUserRoles, assignRole, revokeRole and grantPermission. Deliberate asymmetry on a Redis outage: fails closed for ADMIN/FINANCE/STAFF/SUPPORT/EXAMINER (where the window actually matters) and fails open for ordinary student/teacher traffic, so a Redis blip cannot turn a 15-minute staleness window into a full API outage.

findings.title: OTP hashed with unsalted SHA-256
findings.note: OTP digests are now HMAC-SHA256 under a pepper derived from JWT_ACCESS_SECRET with a domain-separation label, computed lazily so unit tests that never boot an environment still import the module. Refresh-token hashing is deliberately left on plain sha256: a 32-byte random secret is not rainbow-table-able, and rotating it would invalidate every live session. In-flight OTP challenges stop verifying on deploy and expire two minutes later.

findings.title: Genuinely simultaneous duplicate ZarinPal callbacks can get a transient 409 instead of an idempotent 200
findings.note: callback()'s settlement moved into PaymentsService.settleVerified, which retries the Serializable transaction once on P2034 and returns the row the winner committed. The in-transaction guard was widened from `status === PAID` to the full SETTLEABLE check, which the retry path needs: the winner may have committed REFUNDED via returnCapture, and the old check would have flipped it back to PAID and granted a second entitlement.
